name: Source Locative-Complement Construction

dimensions.form: Verb head with a source-denoting PP in locative-complement function, headed centrally by from, away, off, or out
dimensions.meaning: Origin or initial location of motion, derivation, or change
dimensions.function: Locative complement of the verb, bearing the semantic role source
dimensions.distribution: VP-internal with motion and change verbs; compatible with a following goal-role locative complement

1.definition: A VP contains a locative complement bearing the source role, marking the initial location of motion or change
1.details: Source is a semantic role, while locative complement is the CGEL syntactic function. Source complements are generally headed by from, away, off, or out. From takes an NP or locative-PP complement; the inner PP in from under the bed expresses the source location and is not another source complement. Away occurs alone or with a from-PP complement; off occurs alone or with an NP object; out occurs alone or with an of- or from-PP complement (CGEL pp. 257–59, 687).

examples.note: The whole from-PP is the source-role locative complement; the inner PP expresses the source location
Complementless away-PP bearing the source role
Source- and goal-role locative complements co-occurring

constraints.description: The whole source-denoting PP is integrated as a locative complement of the verb, not added as a locative adjunct.
The complement denotes the initial location or state and can co-occur with a separate goal-role locative complement.

projection.target: In their central motion uses, integrated locative PPs headed by from, away, off, or out predict an initial-location construal, head-specific complementation, and compatibility with a separate goal-role complement
projection.evidence: CGEL gives the four-head realization inventory and its distinct complement patterns on p. 687; spatial, state, and possession examples distinguish initial-location source from final-location goal on pp. 258–60

grounds.note: Head choice projects initial-location interpretation, complementation, and source-goal compatibility
The source-role profile recurs across motion, state, and possession domains

core.property: Source role borne by a locative PP complement
diagnostics: integration in a motion or change frame
from, away, off, or out as PP head

known_boundary_items: Away from can express retrospective direction, and off has restricted goal uses; the containing event distinguishes these from the central source uses
path or route complements such as through the tunnel and via Chicago instantiate the distinct path-complement construction
derivational sources such as made from grapes: extension beyond literal motion

relatedConstructions.notes: The source-role locative complement is licensed within VP structure
The source-role locative complement is a PP headed centrally by from, away, off, or out

grounds.note: Source is a semantic role borne by a PP in locative-complement function

curious.title: Saying where something started
curious.summary: A small phrase with from, away, off or out can tell where a movement or change began.
curious.body:
In She came from Toronto, the phrase from Toronto says where the coming started. Phrases beginning with away, off or out do a similar job: Kim jumped off the pier, He came out of the room, She walked away.

This dictionary treats these phrases as built into the verb phrase, not added on as extras. A starting point can also go together with a separate end point, as in They flew from Toronto to Ottawa. This dictionary marks the analysis as provisional.
curious.try: Describe a trip with where it started and where it ended, such as I walked from ... to ...

teacher.summary: Helps explain phrases with from, away, off or out that name the starting point of motion or change.
teacher.explain: Source is a semantic role: the initial location of motion, derivation or change. In CGEL terms, it's borne by a locative complement of the verb, a PP headed by from, away, off or out, integrated into the VP and not added as an adjunct. From takes an NP or locative PP (from under the bed). Away occurs alone or with a from-PP. Off occurs alone or with an NP object. Out occurs alone or with an of-PP or from-PP. A separate goal-role locative complement can follow (from Toronto to Ottawa). This dictionary marks the analysis as provisional.
teacher.terms: In this dictionary, such a phrase is called a source-role locative complement.

contrasts.text: They flew from Toronto to Ottawa.

watch_for: A learner might treat the inner PP in from under the bed as a second source complement, when the whole from-PP is the complement.
A learner might pair away or off with the wrong complement, since each head has its own complement pattern.
teacher.activity: Students trace a route on a map and write sentences using from, away, off and out for starting points. They then add a goal phrase to at least one.

child.hook: How do you say where a trip started?
child.explain: Words like from, off and out can tell where something started. She came from Toronto. Kim jumped off the pier. They flew from Toronto to Ottawa.
child.play: Act out a short trip. Say where you started with from, off or out, and where you ended with to.

checked.note: Fixed: curious body no longer says the verb needs these phrases (the entry says they are integrated complements, not adjuncts, without claiming they are obligatory); teacher summary no longer implies the verb is incomplete without the phrase; removed the traditional-grammar label 'adverbial phrases of place or direction', which the entry does not make and which is broader than the construction.
